what_happened: A 233-line scratch probe restating the whole HistoryMorphism lift chain with the four def:frame constraints as explicit hypotheses compiled clean on the first attempt (lake env lean, exit 0, no warnings), settling the Saturation question mechanically rather than by reading proof terms.

Second probe wrapped StateTopology SeparatingFrame.srel as a FrameOver intOrder via ofReflective; the reflection law is a 3-line abs_sub_comm proof. This yields a concrete non-saturated base frame over Z-time, the non-vacuity witness the weakened chain needs. ConstraintWitnesses.lean's module docstring currently records that no FrameOver wrapper exists for srel because the reflection law is unproved there.

Third probe iteration showed the base frame needs NO def:frame constraint at all, not merely Limit: the chain's step duration delta = intIso.symm 1 is nonzero, so base-side reflection is the definitional reflect_reflection_of_ne rather than reflection_of_limit. Compiles exit 0 with only an unused-binder linter warning.

Four 'Constraints consumed: Compositionality, Seriality, Limit, Saturation' docstrings (HistoryMorphism.lean lines 468, 525, 586 and UniversalCover.lean line 441) over-report: they record the IsRegular binder present on the declaration rather than the constraints the proof actually projects. This over-claim is why the Saturation question looked open. No dispatch blocker; recorded as a plan objective.

The research report shipped two compiled transplant probes (specs/evidence/history-morphism-saturation-audit/), so phase decomposition was transcription from a verified-compiling reference rather than estimation: every new signature in the plan's Lean Challenge Statements block is a signature that already compiled, and each phase's fallback in Rollback/Contingency points at the probe as the reference term. No tactic search or feasibility guessing was needed at plan time.

The research report's step-2 recommendation ('correct the four over-reporting docstrings') reads as repo-wide, but a grep found ~20 occurrences of the same 'Constraints consumed: Compositionality, Seriality, Limit, Saturation' line across FormalSystem/Nomic/, Validity.lean and Correspondence/RigidityReal.lean. Only the 3 in HistoryMorphism.lean and the 1 in UniversalCover.lean are on the audited chain, so the plan names the other ~20 as an explicit Non-Goal to stop the docstring phase from silently widening to a repo-wide audit.

Phase 1 commit blocked by the typst-sync-check.sh pre-commit gate (Check 2, --counts-only): adding declarations to FormalSystem/Semantics/HistoryMorphism.lean changed formalsystem-line-count (committed=395347 vs live=395453), so typst/generated/status.typ drifted. Remedy is 'typst-sync-check.sh --fix' plus staging typst/generated/status.typ. Consequence: typst/generated/status.typ joins the touched-file set on every phase that adds Lean lines, widening the plan's 7-file Phase 6 scope hypothesis to 8.

Phase 1 was transcription rather than proof search: the research report's compiled probe at specs/evidence/history-morphism-saturation-audit/lift-chain-without-isregular.lean supplied every reparameterised proof body verbatim. All three builds (module, nine-module interface tier, full library) were green on the first attempt with zero warnings and no tactic iteration.

Phase 4 additions pushed FormalSystem/Semantics/StateTopology/ConstraintWitnesses.lean from 1757 to 1824 lines, tripping Mathlib's linter.style.longFile against the file's in-source baseline of 1800; bumped the baseline to 1900 per lakefile.toml's documented convention (a file over the package limit carries a tight in-source set_option). Separately, the test-library fixture's fully qualified reference to StateTopology.SeparatingFrame.exists_nonSaturated_base_orientedForest_cover exceeded the 100-char longLine limit; fixed with an 'open ... in' rather than a linter opt-out. Neither was anticipated by the plan.

C16's suggested remedy, 'lake exe runLinter --update FormalSystem', is destructive in this repo: it rewrote scripts/nolints.json from 914 lines to 237, discarding every grandfathered entry not reported by the single root passed on the command line. Restored from a pre-run backup (verified byte-identical to HEAD) and used the in-source '@[nolint unusedArguments]' plus scripts/nolint-attribute-allowlist.txt route instead. Anyone following C16's printed advice verbatim on this repo will silently drop the baseline.
git-commit-scoped.sh dropped 'scripts/check-module-invariants.sh' from a commit pathspec: not contained in task #898's declared file_scope.
git-commit-scoped.sh dropped 'scripts/nolint-attribute-allowlist.txt' from a commit pathspec: not contained in task #898's declared file_scope.

The C16 unusedArguments linter independently corroborated the task's central finding: with both discrete-time lift headlines delegating to the new _of_constraints forms, the linter reports the base frame's [F.IsRegular] binder as unread on both. That is the audited result restated by a tool with no knowledge of the task, and it is stronger evidence than the transplant probe alone.

Phases 1-4 each closed on a green full 'lake build' plus the plan's declared interface-tier dependent builds and gate 4, and all four were committed on that evidence -- but scripts/check-module-invariants.sh, which no phase's Verification Tier named, then reported five failures introduced by exactly those phases (C34 closed-vocabulary markers x12, C34b x3, C34a x1, C15 x2, C16 x2, plus stale INV blocks). A full lake build does not cover the repo's docstring-marker, index-anchoring, or linter-baseline gates. Plans for this repo should name check-module-invariants.sh in the per-phase tier for any phase that edits a Constraints-consumed marker, adds a theorem-index row, or changes which binders a proof reads.
